node.label: Michel Vovelle
node.date_label: Piété baroque et déchristianisation en Provence (1973) · Idéologies et mentalités (1982) · La Mentalité révolutionnaire (article) (1991)
node.description: Historian of collective mentalities and the French Revolution who connected long changes in death and religion to moments of political rupture. In La Mentalité révolutionnaire,Vovelle asks whether slow transformations can accelerate in revolutionary crisis. His analysis treats hope and fear,violence and fraternity as interrelated,and explicitly rejects both unconditional devotion to the Revolution and blanket denunciation.

incident_edges.relationship: Uses Vovelle’s testamentary research as the starting point for a methodological reflection on dechristianization.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Own1975 pp52–56 praises Piété baroque et déchristianisation1973 as a pioneering, rigorous and nuanced inquiry, then examines conclusions drawn from it. At58 he calls quantitative inquiry legitimate and indispensable for the institutional Christianity it measures. Original Vovelle book unread; praise is distinct from total methodological equivalence.

incident_edges.relationship: Distinguishes Vovelle’s quantitative history of religious practice from a qualitative history of different Christian models.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Own1975 pp56–60 explicitly calls this a methodological dialogue, says the chosen dossier is unassailable within its horizons and warns hasty readers against extrapolating religion’s complete disappearance. The comparison is undirected and not a claim Vovelle himself predicted Christianity’s death. Both approaches have distinct objects and can coexist; no manufactured personal quarrel.
